The key is to get it off the lees as soon as primary ferment has finished, then letting it age in the bottle for a minimum of six months to a year.

You need a minimum of 1kg (3 lbs) of fruit per gallon. You can boil fruit without pectin, but cold sterilize the fruit if it's pectin rich, or use pectinase. Don't go crazy on the best honey you can find, but don't use cheap shit either. Add it to the primary ferment, don't listen to people who say add it after - the yeast needs the goodies in the fruit which don't exist in honey itself.

Always always always use either lemons or yeast nutrient - you can't get away without it. add it in stages to keep the ferment going.

Let the mead finish it's ferment and then cold sterilize and backsweeten with honey later. it's always worth waiting the extra time for it to mature.

You're gonna need about 3 lbs of honey for the sugar, but make sure you check the original gravity to make sure it will be a fairly strong wine. DO NOT BOIL THE HONEY as it fucks it up and causes bad flavour. dissolve it in warm, sterile cheap mineral water from the store.
